- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for early spikes.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.40 or above), model often overestimates short-term momentum; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum after 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecasted peak values.
- After a strong upward spike (e.g., >85.00), model often fails to correct downward; apply a 2–3 day lagged mean reversion adjustment.
- When sentiment is low and price is trending down, model tends to forecast a steeper decline; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 10–15 days, model overreacts; apply a 3–5 day smoothing filter to forecast path.
